title: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): scheduling meetings from Copilot Chat in GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold because three descriptions of scheduling go beyond the evidence: Copilot choosing attendees, reading particular people's calendars, and distributing every drafted agenda to every attendee. The roadmap details and Integrated Apps paths are supported, but those additional behaviours need to be removed or framed as questions rather than established facts.

claims.claim: Blocking the app restricts its use for all users in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook, rather than disabling scheduling alone.
claims.quote: You can block an app for all users in your organization to restrict them from downloading and using the app on the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook.

claims.claim: The Specific users/group option limits self-installation and use to the selected users.
claims.quote: Specific users/group in the organization can install means that only the users selected by you are able to install the app on their own from the store and use it in the client. Unselected users are not able to do so.

claims.claim: The availability setting does not affect admin-deployed apps.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own.

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat describes the Integrated Apps block as covering the Copilot app, Teams, Outlook and the web.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.claim: Scheduling from chat hands the choice of attendee list to Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot" "schedule" "attendees" "agenda" "chat" -site:learn.microsoft.com/answers'; read roadmap and August 25 release-note excerpts. They describe scheduling with colleagues, not Copilot deciding whom to invite; email-thread scheduling is a different scenario.
claims.fix: Remove 'attendee list' from the first sentence of Why it matters. The roadmap supports finding times, booking rooms and drafting agendas, but not choosing attendees.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, first bullet
claims.claim: Finding available times draws on calendar information for both the user and the named colleagues.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot" "scheduling" "calendar availability"', '"Copilot" "schedule" calendar details agenda sources confirm send invitation account'; read roadmap, requirements, overview and release-note excerpts. None identifies whose calendars this item reads.
claims.fix: Replace 'Finding available times draws on calendar information for the user and the colleagues named.' with 'The roadmap says Copilot will find available times.' Keep the following question about which calendar details it reads or shows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet
claims.claim: Agendas drafted by this feature go out in invitations to every attendee.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Scheduling with Copilot" "agenda" "source"', '"Copilot" "schedule" "attendees" "agenda" "chat" -site:learn.microsoft.com/answers'; read roadmap and release-note excerpts. Drafting agendas and sending invites are stated, but this distribution guarantee is not.
claims.fix: Replace 'Agendas Copilot drafts go out in invitations to every attendee.' with 'Review any agenda included in a proposed invitation before sending it.' This frames the point as advice rather than an undocumented distribution guarantee.
